w: Swamishri performed the ground-breaking ceremony for a new assembly hall at the mandir complex in Navsari.

During the morning assembly, Swamishri explained, "... You have all experienced the worldly pleasures and luxuries of life. To add further, this soul has also become Indra and enjoyed the mundane pleasures. In spite of all this still there is no satisfaction. The more you indulge the more your desires grow. If you put ghee in fire then the fire will not die out but increase all the more. Likewise, by indulging in worldly pleasures, there is no reason to believe one will become satisfied. One can only become desireless through the refuge and association of the Satpurush (holy guru)..."
Swamishri departed from Navsari at 6.00 p.m.
Balaks and kishores sang bhajans in Swamishri's morning puja

At 10.45 am, Swamishri met Sheikh Hamed Bin Majid Al-Qassimi - Minister of Justice of UAE and cousin brother of the Sheikh of Sharjah - Sheikh Dr. Sultan. Sheikh Hamed welcomed Swamishri in his palace in Sharjah. He was impressed on learning of Swamishri's effort in inspiring morality and peace in society. The Sheikh said, "You are doing good work. Spreading world peace can be done through saints like you ... I hope this will not be our last meeting. I wish that we meet again and again." Before departing Swamishri presented the Sheikh with an Amrut Kalash as a memento.

In the evening, the balaks and kishores presented a program of speeches and narration on incidents from the life of Swamishri. In his blessings Swamishri recollected incidents about Shastriji Maharaj and Yogiji Maharaj.

Many sadhus and devotees were eagerly awaiting in a hall for Swamishri’s arrival for dinner. Swamishri entered with folded hands and proceeded in that manner all the way to his seat. Someone asked, “Why fold your hands all the way?”

Swamishri responded, “God resides in all so one has to fold one’s hands.” Then Swamishri added, “I follow what Shastriji Maharaj has taught me. He told me to fold my hands before all. One should get work done by folding one’s hands. Then one will experience divine feelings and glory for all and have personal joy.”
Swamishri’s humility is forever a source of inspiration to all.

A special assembly of devotees, who had reformed from their wayward and lawless means, was held today. They came from Bhangadh, 17 km from Dholera (120 km from Amdavad), and twelve neighbouring villages, namely, Goghla, Khun, Mahadevpura, Mingalpur, Gandhipura, Rahtalav, Jhankhi, Mundi, Kamatalav, Sarasla, Shela and Devpura. They are farmers by occupation, but because of droughts, addictions, superstitions and bad customs their lives had declined morally. Then through the blessings of Swamishri, BAPS sadhus started regular satsang visits to the villages. Through the inspiration of Swamishri the BAPS built a school and hostel for children in Bhangadh. Thereafter, the efforts of leading locals of the region, namely, Aniruddhsinh, Arunbhai Trivedi (secretary of Bhanumala Trust), Dr L.P. Shukla and Dr Sharadbhai Thakkar, played an important role in transforming the villagers. A small medical clinic was also set up by the Sanstha. To appreciate the change in the locals and the efforts of the leading lights an assembly was arranged today in Sarangpur. Dr Sharadbhai Thakkar, Sagarbhai Solanki, administrator of Pramukh Swami Maharaj Vidyamandir (school) and Pramukh Kumar Chhatralay (hostel) in Bhangadh, Chandubhai, chief of Bhangadh village, Hariombhai Chauhan, a social worker, and Arunbhai Trivedi, secretary of Bhanumala Trust expressed their feelings in the assembly.

Finally, Swamishri blessed the assembly, “We have heard the wonderful reformations that have been effected in the lives of people. Bhagwan Swaminarayan and his sadhus had reformed the lives of thousands who were under the vice-grip of addictions and bad customs. This mission of moralizing people is still being continued today. The sadhus seek to unshackle people from addictions, to purify their souls and to engage them in devotion to God. Bhagwan Swaminarayan has preached “Dharmo gneyaha sadacharaha” – to live a life of dharma free from addictions, gambling, violence, etc. If there are no morals in life then a person cannot do good things.”

Girishbhai Patel, owner of Sterling Hospital, came to receive Pramukh Swami Maharaj's blessings. He said to Swamishri, "After seeing Akshardham here and the mandir in London, and seeing the themes of that mandir, I became convinced in my heart that such a Sampraday is very much needed for society. Everything that society needs is here. Here there is religion along with science. I also understand that science is not everything. It also needs religion, and if science is brought together with the strength that religion has, society will progress. After seeing this, I have come for your darshan."
After his meal, Pramukh Swami Maharaj sat to read letters. Meanwhile a phone call came from Madhubhai in America. The attendant sadhu took the phone to Swamishri.

Madhubhai's only son, a young man named Akshar, had passed away to Akshardham. In 1998, after his bypass surgery, Swamishri had stayed in West Chester at the home of Dr Mahendrabhai and his brothers Madhubhai, Ashokbhai and Bharatbhai. As Swamishri himself said, since then a close, family-like bond had formed. Madhubhai's son Akshar was living in New York and studying at college. He lived alone in a house in New York and had had some heart trouble from before, and he suddenly died of heart failure. A few days earlier, when Madhubhai and Mahendrabhai gave Swamishri the news of their only son's passing, Swamishri was lying on his bed at 10:30. Even as they gave the news, the ring of their faith in Swamishri could be heard in their words. Even then they had said, "Bapa! Akshar was yours and you have taken him, so we feel no grief at all. We are convinced that he has gone straight to Akshardham." Swamishri too had been pleased to see their faith and understanding.

Also, because of some other arrangements there, the cremation was delayed. In the days in between, they had held a parayan (a series of scriptural readings). At the parayan, Madhubhai offered penda as prasad every day. The volunteers also saw that Madhubhai's wife had the same wonderful understanding. She too was just as composed. Today, when Akshar was cremated, the family held a special assembly at the crematorium. A very large number of people came to this assembly, from local satsangis to their relatives. Before the cremation, everyone in the assembly spoke only of their joy and faith in having attained a guru like Pramukh Swami Maharaj. Not only that, as Akshar's body was being pushed into the electric furnace, his elder sister stood up and spoke, addressing Akshar himself: "Akshar! Mummy has asked me to tell you that after you finished college, it was our responsibility to get you married with great celebration, but now that is not possible. Yet for us there is even greater joy today, because today you are going to be wedded to Parabrahman Bhagwan Swaminarayan himself. What greater joy and celebration could there be than this?" His young sister spoke completely calmly, without tears in her eyes, from her inner faith, while everyone present in the crematorium had tears in their eyes. Penda were handed out to all, but no one had the heart to eat them. Only three people were composed: Madhubhai, his wife and his daughter.

When the attendant sadhu told Swamishri what the devotees had related, Swamishri too was choked with emotion. His face filled with feeling and the corners of his eyes filled with tears. Swamishri took the phone in his hand, but for a few moments he could not speak.

Madhubhai said to Swamishri, "Bapa! Akshar has passed away, but no one here has cried, no one is grieving. We have kept the understanding that Akshar has gone straight to Akshardham, and today Akshar's cremation went well. The festival went well."

Swamishri said, "You all have satsang and firm understanding, so you are at peace. We also say that he has gone straight to Akshardham. Everyone has firm knowledge and understanding, and our blessing is that it grows even more."
Madhubhai said, "It is your love. Akshar left having earned your pleasure. Bless us that we too may earn your love and pleasure in the same way."
Swamishri said, "We stayed at your home for two months, so a family-like feeling had formed."
Madhubhai said, "By your grace the cremation went well."
Hearing this, Swamishri said in a voice full of emotion, "Any occasion in the life of a devotee of God is a festival."

Girishbhai Patel, owner of Sterling Hospital, came to receive Swamishri's blessings. He said to Swamishri, "After seeing Akshardham here and the mandir in London, and seeing the themes of the mandir, I became convinced inside that such a sampraday is very necessary for society. Everything society needs is here. Here there is dharma along with science. I too understand that science is not everything. It needs dharma too, and if science is united with the power that lies in dharma, society will rise. After seeing this I have come for your darshan."
After the meal Swamishri sat to read letters. Meanwhile a call came from Madhubhai in America. The attendant sadhu took the phone to Swamishri.

Madhubhai's only son, the young Akshar, had passed away. In 1998, after his bypass surgery, Swamishri had stayed in West Chester at the homes of Dr. Mahendrabhai and his brothers Madhubhai, Ashokbhai and Bharatbhai. As Swamishri says, since then a family like closeness had formed. Madhubhai's son Akshar was studying at college in New York. Living alone in a house in New York, he had always had some heart trouble, and he passed away from sudden heart failure. When Madhubhai and Mahendrabhai gave Swamishri the news of their only son's passing a few days earlier, Swamishri was lying on his bed at 10:30. Even while giving the news, the ring of faith in Swamishri could be heard in their words. Even then they had said, "Bapa! Akshar was yours and you have taken him, so we have no sorrow of any kind. We are sure he has taken his seat in Akshardham." Swamishri too was pleased to see their faith and understanding.

Because of some other arrangements there, the cremation was delayed. In the days in between they held a parayan. Every day during the parayan Madhubhai offered penda (sweets) as prasad. The volunteers especially experienced the wonderful understanding of his wife, just like Madhubhai's. She too was just as calm. Today, when Akshar was cremated, the family held a special assembly at the crematorium. A very large number came to it, from local satsangis to relatives. In the assembly before the cremation they all spoke only of the joy and faith of having a guru like Pramukh Swami Maharaj. Not only that: as Akshar's body was being moved into the electric furnace, his elder sister stood up and spoke to Akshar himself: "Akshar! Mummy has asked me to tell you that after you finished college, as our duty, we were going to marry you off with great celebration. That is not possible now, but in our hearts there is even greater joy today, because you are going today to wed the manifest Parabrahman Swaminarayan Bhagwan. What greater joy and celebration could there be?" As his young sister spoke this calmly, without tears, from the faith in her heart, everyone in the crematorium had tears in their eyes. Penda were handed out to all, but no one had the heart to eat them. Only three people were calm: Madhubhai, his wife and their daughter.

When the attendant sadhu told Swamishri what the devotees had related, Swamishri too was choked with emotion. His face was filled with feeling and the corners of his eyes filled up. Swamishri took the phone, but for a few moments could not speak.

Madhubhai again said to Swamishri, "Bapa! Akshar has passed away, but no one has wept after him; no one is in sorrow. We have kept the understanding that Akshar has taken his seat in Akshardham, and today Akshar's cremation went well. The celebration went well."

Swamishri said, "There is satsang in all of you and firm understanding, so there is peace. We too say that he has taken his seat in God's abode. Everyone has firmness of knowledge and understanding, and my blessings are that it grows even more."
Madhubhai said, "You love us. Akshar left with your pleasure; please bless us so that we too receive your love and pleasure in the same way."
Swamishri said, "We stayed at your home for two months, so a feeling just like family had formed."
Madhubhai said, "By your grace the cremation went well."
Hearing this, with words full of feeling, Swamishri said, "Every occasion of a devotee of God is a celebration."

Two brothers had not been speaking to each other for a long time. Both are satsangis and sensible too, but the gulf between their views could not be bridged in any way. But today, in keeping with Mahant Swami Maharaj's wish, the two brothers had reconciled.

One of the brothers was present here now. Seeing him, Swamishri was overjoyed and embraced him. He gave him many blessings. The brother who was not present here was phoned. Swamishri blessed him too over the phone. The sadhus told him, "Swamishri was very pleased and embraced your brother."
The sadhus touched the phone to Swamishri's chest and said, "Showing his pleasure with you too, Swamishri is embracing you through the phone."
There was joy on Swamishri's face as if he were embracing him in person.
Swamishri shows his wish for unity on every occasion, but when he sees unity embodied, he showers his grace without limit.
Roshan, a young man travelling with him for the seva of letter writing, asked Mahant Swami Maharaj, "What should we do so that there is peace within and no one's words hurt us?"
Swamishri answered, "Thinking of who the doer is. Thinking of who the doer is, is the master key."

Today a meeting had been arranged between Mahant Swami Maharaj and the President of Uganda, Shri Museveniji. Swamishri arrived at the reception room of State House at 12.05. The President was yet to come. The waiting went on until 2.10 in the afternoon, but there was still no news of the meeting. Everyone's faith and patience were now running out, but not Swamishri's!
Swamishri said, "Even if he takes his time to meet us, we will take him to Akshardham at once; we will not take our time."
Just then news came that the President had gone out and had only just come back.
Swamishri immediately exclaimed, "Then when will he eat?"
When one is going through such a trying situation oneself, would anyone think of another like this?! Though at that moment there was no opportunity to look into all this.

Then the meeting began, and in it Atmaswarupdas Swami told the President, "You came after two o'clock, and when Swamishri learned that you had not yet eaten, Swamishri asked, 'When will the President eat?'"
Hearing this, the President was overcome with emotion and said, "Swamishri cares so much about me!"
From then until he came out, he kept holding Swamishri's hand.

ds.t: May Bhagwan do good to all
w: When Mahant Swami Maharaj returned to his residence after meeting the President, it had become very late. At everyone's request, Swamishri went to bed. While talking, Swamishri sat up in bed and said, "Seeing all the people on the way, I was thinking: Bhagwan, do good to all. Bhagwan, do good to all."
All the sadhus were astounded. What a wonderful person this is! Always ignoring his own troubles, he keeps thinking only of doing good to others!
Today, while Mahant Swami Maharaj's head was being shaved, talk turned to bitter experiences of getting cut.
Swamishri said, "It happened to us too, in Dharmaj. There was an old man who came to us. It was winter. It was 4.30 in the morning, and his hands were trembling..."
The sadhus said, "So was the shaving done?"
Swamishri laughed and said, "Eight cuts." That is, there were eight cuts during that shave.
The sadhus said, "Oh my..."
Swamishri said, "The record is seventeen cuts, in Sarangpur."
Giving the reason for it, he said, "Our turn came after sixteen sadhus, didn't it? By then the razor would have become blunt!"

The thought came to mind: how much the great sadhu must have endured like this! To please someone, to fulfil someone's wish, and above all to make all of us understand, "Brother! In life you will have to endure."
